title: MeReader: An Offline, Privacy-Preserving, Progress-Aware AI Assistant for Narrative eBook Reading
abstract: arXiv:2611.18513v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: This paper introduces MeReader, a privacy-preserving, offline and progress-aware AI assistant designed to function as a contextual companion for narrative reading on consumer hardware. Unlike conventional Large Language Model (LLM)-based systems that process documents/books online in an all-texts-at-once type of way, thereby risking narrative spoilers, MeReader confines both retrieval and generation to the reader's distinct position in the text. The system integrates a hybrid retrieval architecture, combining vector similarity, BM25, and summary embeddings, to ensure high fidelity to the reader's current context. We evaluate the system across classical English books using both quantitative comprehension metrics and qualitative LLM-based independent judging. translated_title: MeReader：面向叙事类电子书阅读的离线、隐私保护、进度感知AI助手
translated_abstract: 本文介绍了MeReader，这是一个隐私保护、离线且进度感知的AI助手，旨在作为消费级硬件上叙事阅读的上下文伴侣。与传统的基于大语言模型（LLM）的系统不同——后者以一次性处理全部文本的方式在线处理文档/书籍，从而存在叙事剧透的风险——MeReader将检索和生成都限制在读者在文本中的具体阅读位置。该系统集成了混合检索架构，结合向量相似度、BM25和摘要嵌入，以确保对读者当前上下文的高保真度。我们使用定量理解指标和基于LLM的定性独立评审，在经典英文书籍上对该系统进行了评估。结果确定了一个质量-延迟边界，表明中等规模的本地模型（2b-4b）可以在保持可接受（延迟）的同时，达到与更大模型（5b+）相当的理解能力。
tldr: MeReader是一个离线、隐私保护且进度感知的电子书阅读AI助手，通过混合向量相似度、BM25与摘要嵌入的检索架构，将内容检索与生成严格限制在读者当前阅读进度内以避免剧透，并证明2b-4b的中等规模本地模型可在可接受延迟下达到与更大模型相当的理解能力。
en_tdlr: MeReader is an offline, privacy-preserving, progress-aware AI assistant for narrative eBook reading that confines retrieval and generation to the reader's current position via a hybrid retrieval architecture (vector similarity, BM25, and summary embeddings), showing that mid-sized local models (2b-4b) achieve comprehension parity with larger models while maintaining acceptable latency.
